1.explanation:
1. We import Carbon’s CSS and the `<Button>` component from `carbon-components-react`.
2. Render three buttons of types `danger`, `danger--tertiary`, and `danger--ghost` side by side. By default, Carbon only applies visual styling for danger states.
3. A screen reader will announce only the button text and won’t convey the semantic danger state.
4. To reproduce the bug, run this code in a React environment (e.g. create-react-app) and navigate through the buttons with a screen reader.
5. The “FixedApp” example adds a visually hidden `<span>` with `id="danger-info"` and sets `aria-describedby="danger-info"` on the button so that assistive technology reads “Primary Danger, Danger!” to communicate the danger state.
1.bug_scenario: In our application we render several Carbon `<Button>` components with `kind="danger"`, `kind="danger--tertiary"`, and `kind="danger--ghost"`. Visually these buttons appear in red to warn users of a destructive action, but when a screen reader focuses on them it only announces their label (e.g. “Danger Button”) and does not communicate that they are in a danger state. The second screenshot shows a proposed fix of adding a visually hidden `<span>` with an `id` and referencing it via `aria-describedby` on the button, but our current implementation does not include this.
